authorised_by: the user, who directed that restarting on error is acceptable
evidence_handling: A point whose evidence file already exists finished its work and died before journalling. It is completed from the durable evidence rather than re-run, so no sealed data is read twice and no evidence file is written twice.
found_at_phase: field close preparation, before the first sealed read
prior_behaviour: recover_interrupted_points turned every started-without-terminal point into a permanent zero with reason interrupted-after-durable-start. An in-process organizer error journals observation-paused and resumes cleanly, but a hard kill -- OOM, power loss, Ctrl-C -- writes nothing, so an unattended ten-hour run that died at hour six would have DNF'd whichever point was in flight.
title: a hard interruption is resumable; a candidate failure still is not
what_did_not_change: A candidate failure is still a permanent zero and can never be retried. CandidateFailureError settles its terminal record inside observe_point before any interruption can occur, so such a point is never in the interrupted set. This is the distinction that actually carries the integrity guarantee, and the test asserts it directly rather than asserting only that restart works.
why_it_does_not_apply_here: Observation is silent, and this was verified rather than assumed. observe_point returns {'status': 'point-terminal'} and nothing else; the score is written to the private stage and the journal records only an evidence_sha256. An interrupted point therefore tells the organizer nothing about its outcome, so re-running it cannot be outcome-shopping. The guard was costing a rerun it never bought.
why_the_old_rule_existed: To stop an organizer who sees a bad partial result from killing the run and retrying until a lane scores better.
